liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alligator** (4 reviews, 1 other source): The reviewer says the Alligator into Caution sequence has long been a setlist puzzle, including whether Bill Graham handled their closing; Reviewer calls the Alligator instrumental a neat little tune [1][4][9][12][15]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Jerry's busy, ever-present guitar work on this one; Short but energetic, with a notable meltdown section [9][12]
- **Cold Rain and Snow** (2 reviews): Before this song, Bobby is heard revealing details about his family life in an interview clip; The instrumental break, normally a Jerry and Pigpen unison part, is judged a disaster with stray harmonica-like noise [6][12]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Beatles aren't here**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd67-06-18.sbd.mandrake.19586.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 5 songs; 40 min; rated 4.31/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals are strong, though at times they come across rough; Reviewer finds the sound good quality and the jams blazing, despite the harmonica; Recording quality is remarkably good, better than expected for a 1967 tape [9][10][15]
- **gd67-06-18.sbd.hollister.42.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 35 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [3]. Said about its sound: Sound is sometimes muddy, especially on Jerry's solos, but still recommended [7]
- **gd1967-06-18.115858.sbd.kaplan.flac16**: soundboard; 5 songs; 41 min; rated 2.3/5 by 10 [2]

## Around the show

- Each track opens with interview excerpts from assorted speakers [6]
- Described as the first big rock festival, with acid widely available among the audience [8]
- Someone on stage plays harmonica tunelessly in the wrong key, and nobody removes him [10]
- The band were angry at being pressured to sign a filming release just before going on stage [14]
- Reviewer hears the band maturing into a tight unit, with roots of Southern guitar bands, Santana and Deep Purple [7]
- Reviewer ranks the set above everything else at the festival except Jimi, with jamming then unheard of [8]
- Because of the release dispute, this set is absent from the festival film, unlike other performers [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd67-06-18.sbd.mandrake.19586.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Mandrake; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: No cassette generation sits between the master reel and DAT, unlike the earlier circulating version; remastered by Mandrake [1]
- **gd67-06-18.sbd.hollister.42.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by D. Hollister; source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1967-06-18.115858.sbd.kaplan.flac16**: transferred by Seth Kaplan; source: Lineage: SBD Master Reels > DAT (Panasonic 3700) > Delta DiO 2496 > PC hard drive > CDR > CDWAV > Cool Edit > Traders Little Helper [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Monterey Fairgrounds - June 18, 1967](https://www.dead.net/show/june-18-1967) [17]
